reference: Native Go 1.27.3 with google.golang.org/adk v1.9.0 (its own Runner and agents) run against a scripted caller by go/conformance
requestReference: The native lane records the wire requests the galaxie model package builds from ADK's LLMRequest; the page-side validators and the router are independent code
lanes: Node galaxie adk-go adapter with the reference module
real headless Chromium galaxie adk-go adapter under the strict mock-mode CSP (every case)
refusedShapes: A tool made by `agenttool` wrapping an agent
An agent made directly with `llmagent.New`, `agent.New` or another ADK constructor instead of the galaxie constructors
A function tool or toolset made directly with ADK instead of a galaxie capability tool
A pause inside a Parallel branch, a Loop iteration or a Sequential child that is not the last one (ADK resumes only the agent that paused, so the siblings would be skipped)
An unbounded Loop with no iteration limit and no exit tool
evidenceOutsideTheCases: go/galaxie/shapes_test.go: each refused construction fails `unsupported` before any model or capability call

tests/conformance/adk-go-agents.node.test.ts: Parallel write branches keep branch-local effect scopes whichever branch reaches the broker first, and a restore after the pause that follows a Parallel stage runs no branch write again
normalizations: Function-call IDs on the wire are assigned by the Go model package (call-<n>) because ADK strips its own IDs from history; scripted replies use their own IDs and the transcripts compare the assigned ones.
Run errors compare by galaxie error code.
Requests are compared as parsed JSON, so key order never decides a comparison.
A case marked unordered runs sibling branches at once, so the three wire lists are compared in the order of their canonical JSON text instead of arrival order.
